source: John's AI-L07 golden labels and rubric (Learning AI-L07, 26/11/2026) and the AI-L15 review; decision 27/11/2026 (Hub row 299): one RAIDD table under the minutes' topics, rules shared by prj01-R1 US-4 (minutes) and US-5 (RAIDD proposals).

types.label: Risk
types.definition: Something that has not happened and may happen, and would hurt the project if it did (a chance of a late date, an extra cost, a lost slot).

types.label: Assumption
types.definition: Something the plan takes as true without proof yet (a date, a duration, an approval expected by a date).

types.label: Issue
types.definition: A problem that is true now and needs handling (over budget, too few bids, a defect found, a shortage that exists today).

types.label: Dependency
types.definition: Work that cannot start or finish until another party or piece of work delivers (a handover, an API, another team's slot).

types.label: Decision
types.definition: A choice the meeting made or confirmed, said as settled (approved, agreed, decided).

changes.definition: Raised for the first time in this meeting.
Changes, confirms or closes an item raised before (the meeting says it was discussed earlier, revised, now different, resolved, delivered, confirmed).

rules: An action (who does what, by when) is not a RAIDD entry: it stays in the topic's actions.
A status report, a figure or a plan detail on its own is not a RAIDD entry unless it carries one of the five types.
Small talk, technical trouble and planned leave that the plan already absorbs are not RAIDD entries.
An assumption that turns out false becomes an issue (an update of the assumption when it was raised before).
A risk that happens becomes an issue; a risk that goes away is an update that closes it.
When the same item comes up in several topics, it is one row: give the topic where it was settled and quote the line that says it most clearly.
A risk names what may happen and its effect; a vague worry with neither is not a risk.
An item about another project is kept only when this meeting discussed it for this project.
